Read and write tines schemas and multiverses to YAML files

Source: R/read-write.R
read-write.Rd

write_tines() writes a schema (or a multiverse) to YAML, and read_tines() reads it back.

A schema's data reference is written under meta.data, with a file path stored relative to the YAML file, so the two can be moved or shared together. A schema whose data was given as a data frame has no reference to write; supply the data again with read_tines(path, data = ).

When a mapped schema is read, it is checked against its data: the columns are looked up (never the data itself) and each step's inputs are checked with validate_schema(). A plain schema has nothing to check against the data, so its data is not touched. If the data comes from an R script, running it means running code from the file, so validate decides whether that happens.

Usage

write_tines(x, path = NULL, ...)

read_tines(path, data = NULL, validate = c("ask", "always", "never"), ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class schema or multiverse.

path

A single string specifying the file path. Optional for write_tines().

...

Arguments passed on to yaml::as.yaml() or yaml::read_yaml().

data

Optional. Data to check the schema against instead of the one the file references; see update_data() for the forms it takes.

validate

How to handle a data source that is an R script: "ask" (the default) asks in an interactive session and skips the check otherwise, "always" runs it without asking, and "never" skips looking up the data's columns altogether.

Value

write_tines() invisibly returns path, and read_tines() returns an object of class schema or multiverse.

Examples

schema <- example_hdi()
temp_path <- withr::local_tempfile(fileext = ".yml")
write_tines(schema, temp_path)
#> ✔ File saved: /tmp/RtmpKSp3wS/file1b3e77f35da8.yml
schema_read <- read_tines(temp_path)

# a mapped schema, checked against a data frame on read
my_data <- data.frame(age = c(25, 30, 35), income = c(50000, 60000, 70000))
mapped <- build_schema("Income") |>
  add_step(
    id = "step-log", decision = "log-transform income",
    inputs = "income", outputs = "log_income"
  )
write_tines(mapped, temp_path)
#> ✔ File saved: /tmp/RtmpKSp3wS/file1b3e77f35da8.yml
read_tines(temp_path, data = my_data)
#> # A schema: Income
#> # Data:     a data frame (not written to file)
#>   id       objective decision             rationale inputs    outputs  
#>   <chr>    <chr>     <chr>                <chr>     <list>    <list>   
#> 1 step-log ""        log-transform income ""        <chr [1]> <chr [1]>
